prompt.brief: Design a regulated credit-scoring ML platform that trains on historical repayment data, handles class imbalance, serves explainable decisions, monitors drift and fairness, and supports model governance.
successSignals: Version source snapshots, feature definitions, labels, training code, model artifacts, approvals, and decision explanations.
Prevent leakage and sampling bias, evaluate imbalanced outcomes and subgroup fairness, and preserve reproducible training lineage.
Gate deployment on offline metrics, explainability, stability, policy approval, and challenger comparison.
Explain PII controls, adverse-action reasons, drift, appeals, rollback, retention, and independent audit access.

functional: Create governed datasets, train and evaluate candidates, compare subgroup metrics, and register approved model versions.
Score an application with a bounded online feature lookup and return a decision, reason codes, model version, and trace.
Support human review, appeals, adverse-action notices, monitoring, rollback, deletion requests, and compliance reports.
nonFunctional: Target AUC-ROC above 0.85 only as one measure; also enforce decision latency below 200 ms and fairness thresholds.
Scale training and evaluation separately from online scoring, with tenant and model-version isolation.
Never serve an unapproved or unverifiable model; make feature reads, decisions, and report generation traceable.
Fall back to the last approved model or manual review when features, registry, or a new model is unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Train on millions of applications, serve 50,000 scoring requests per second, and retain governed evidence for seven years.
Partition training data and telemetry by model version, time, and tenant; isolate large backfills.
Retain encrypted feature snapshots, labels, explanations, approvals, and decisions while minimizing online state.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Regulated credit-scoring ML platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Regulated credit-scoring ML platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Regulated credit-scoring ML platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Regulated credit-scoring ML platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Regulated credit-scoring ML platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Regulated credit-scoring ML platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Regulated credit-scoring ML platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Regulated credit-scoring ML platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Regulated credit-scoring ML platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines data lineage, imbalanced learning, explainability, fairness, publication, and failure contracts.
Entities and applicant/run/model keys support credit scoring, fairness, privacy, audit, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Regulated credit-scoring ML platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
